text:
Marathon Petroleum bounced back 3.9% today after a brutal two-week slide of nearly 13%, likely getting support from renewed geopolitical tension in the Middle East. The drone attack on Kuwait and inflammatory rhetoric from Iran raised concerns about potential disruption to oil flows in a region critical to global supply, which typically lifts refiner margins — the profit spread between crude oil costs and product prices. With US refineries running at 97.5% capacity and storage levels moderate, any supply shock would tighten the market in ways that favor processors like Marathon.

The broader context here is mixed. The collapse of climate talks at COP31 — specifically the removal of language calling for phasing out fossil fuels — removes a near-term regulatory threat that had likely weighed on the stock during the two-week decline. However, the pending Dangote Refinery IPO in Africa and Saudi Arabia's pivot toward more efficient spending signal long-term headwinds for refining margins globally, as new capacity and conservative investment spending will eventually moderate the profit environment.
